chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who went out during the month of Ramadan while his companions were eating their pre-dawn meal (suhoor) in a house. He looked at the dawn and called out to them. Some of them refrained, but some of them thought he was joking, so he ate. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He completes his fast and makes up for it (qada).'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone eats after dawn because they thought the call to prayer was a joke?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia principle of 'presumption of continuity' (istishab) in fasting, where the fast remains valid despite doubt or misinterpretation of the dawn call. The requirement for qada (making up the day) rather than kaffarah (expiation) highlights the distinction between unintentional error and deliberate breaking, reflecting the juristic emphasis on ease and avoiding undue hardship for the believer.
